messages:
lucy: Heads-up — saw a steady trickle of fncall schema rejects from the invoice-ocr route starting ~07:40 UTC. ~60 rejects in 30m, mostly validator:type_mismatch and enum_unknown.
patrick: Are these coming from the same model variant? Could be newer client sending different enum values.
anita: Quick check: route config shows schema v2.1, several customers still on client v1.8 which uses an older enum set.
ryan: Current runtime behavior: strict validation rejects with 400 and increments fncall.schema.rejects metric. No DLQ or payload retention. That means limited signal to debug patterns across orgs.
lucy: Proposal: add opt-in DLQ for fncall rejects, with per-route sample rate, per-org retention, and redaction. Keep default off. Also add a "permissive fallback" routing option that, when enabled, forwards requests to a permissive schema variant instead of rejecting.
patrick: Console UX question: how do we present both options without confusing customers? I suggest two toggles in route settings: "Enable DLQ (sample %)" and "Permissive fallback (auto-fallback %)". Hover explains risk of masking bugs.
anita: Telemetry needs: fncall.schema.rejects.count, fncall.schema.rejects.pct, fncall.dlq.stored.count, fncall.fallback.used.count. Tag by org_id, route, validator_code, variant. Export sampled payloads as encrypted objects and index metadata for quick queries (no raw payload in logs).
ryan: Security constraints: DLQ objects should be envelope-encrypted. If customer supplies a KMS key use that; otherwise platform key. Replays must run in a sandbox that disables network egress and external tool invocation. Replays flagged as "diagnostic" and not billed to customer by default.
lucy: Example route config draft:
{ "route": "invoice-ocr", "schema": "v2.1", "dlq": {"enabled": "true", "sample_pct": "0.5", "retention_days": "30"}, "permissive_fallback": {"enabled": "false", "percent": "0"} }
patrick: Rollout strategy: behind FF fncall_dlq_plus_fallback. Steps: internal org + dev sandbox -> 5 pilot partners -> 1% sampling across hosted customers -> Console GA. Keep permissive fallback default off unless org explicitly opts in.
anita: Billing: if customer turns on 100% DLQ + replay, we need a quota/credit model. Add a diagnostic_replay_credits field on org config, default 0 for free tier. Replays should decrement credits unless customer opts to be billed.
ryan: Alerting: create an incident rule: if schema.rejects.pct > 0.5% for 10m AND absolute rejects > 50 in 10m, create a ticket and ping route owner. Also surface a "DLQ recommended" hint in Console when rejects persist.
lucy: UI detail: DLQ viewer shows list of recent samples (redacted) with quick filters: validator_code, org_id, client_version, timestamp. Provide "export as encrypted bundle" button and a replay action (disabled unless user has Replayer role).
patrick: Implementation notes: DLQ writes must be async/nonblocking. Add a small DLQ service that applies redaction → encrypt → store (S3) and indexes metadata in Dynamo. Keep the write path < 5ms extra latency.
anita: Edgecases: streaming fncalls — capture the assembled final object plus last valid partial states. Also for multi-part toolcalls, store correlation id so replays can reproduce sequence in order.
ryan: Quick security callout: replays should never call customer-supplied webhooks or third-party tools. If a replay attempts to invoke a tool, simulator should stub responses or run in a fake tool harness.
anita: Telemetry tag proposal: dlq:true|false, dlq_sample:true|false, fallback:true|false, validator:missing_field|type_mismatch|enum_unknown, client_version:semver. That should make filtering easy.
lucy: Action items: Lucy to write RFC and request feature flag; Ryan to prototype DLQ service + sandboxed replay runner; Anita to design Console DLQ/fallback UI and telemetry schema; Patrick to draft rollout + billing credit model.
infra-bot: deploy: fncall-validator v3.2 deployed to eu-central-1; smoke checks OK.
patrick: thanks — ping me when RFC is up and i'll schedule privacy + product sync.
lucy: will do. Thanks team :thumbsup:
